introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0550 Geography 1, June 2021, Ordinary Level, General Certificate of Education Board). Answer ALL questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; decide which one is correct and mark only one answer for each question (marking more than one answer scores zero for that question). Calculators are allowed. Time allowed: one and a half (1½) hours. Mobile phones are not allowed in the examination room.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D. Questions 1-4 refer to one contour map; Questions 13-15 refer to one climate table; Question 31 is a multiple-completion question (one or more responses may be correct); Questions 32-35 give two statements each; Questions 44-46 refer to one sketch map of Cameroon.

Square grid of four columns and four rows with eastings 45 to 49 along the top and bottom and northings 99 to 03 along the sides; a shaded square, a cross and the label sch are drawn in some squares (Question 5).

Two identical sketches of land (hatched, left) and sea (right) with a dashed loop of air marked by the letters W (over the land), Y (top), X (over the sea, with the label WINDS) and Z (bottom); the lower sketch is labelled Q.11 Set B (Questions 11-12).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 1 to 4. Study the contour map below (north is at the top; contour lines are labelled 200, about 110 and 80; places A and B are marked).

![fig-1](gce-ol-geography-2021-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

If the vertical interval of the map above is 10 m, state the height of the place "A" marked.

*Options as printed:* A) 260 m.   B) 265 m.   C) 270 m.   D) 280 m.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The contour labelled 200 gives the reference height. The labels fall to 80 in the south-east corner, so the ground rises towards the north-west. Count the contour lines from the 200 m contour towards A: each line adds the vertical interval of 10 m, giving 210, 220, 230, 240, 250 and 260 m. A stands on the sixth contour above the 200 m line, so its height is 200 + 6 × 10 = 260 m. 270 m is the reading of a candidate who counts one contour too many (the label 200 is written between two neighbouring lines), 280 m two too many, and 265 m would need a point half-way between two contours.

**Intended answer: A (260 m).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Refer to the contour map given with Question 1.

To move from B to A you likely will:

*Options as printed:* A) Ascend.   B) Descend.   C) Cross a road.   D) Go to the east.
questions.corrige_markdown:
On this map the heights fall towards the south-east (200 m in the middle, 80 m at the south-east corner), so the ground rises towards the north-west corner where B stands. B lies beyond the highest contour drawn in that corner, at least six contours (about 60 m) higher than A. Going from B to A therefore means going down the slope: you descend. No road is drawn on the map, so option C is ruled out. A is also to the east (and a little south) of B, so option D is true as a direction, but a contour map is used to tell the change of height, which is what the question asks.

**Intended answer: B (Descend).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Refer to the contour map given with Question 1.

In what direction would farmers make their ridges to prevent soil erosion?
questions.corrige_markdown: Ridges built along the contour lines (across the slope) hold the rainwater and let it soak into the soil instead of running downhill and carrying the soil away. On the map the contour lines run from the south-west to the north-east (the north arrow points to the top of the page), while the slope runs from north-west to south-east. The ridges should therefore run NE-SW. Ridges running NW-SE or NW would go up and down the slope and would channel the water, starting gullies; N-S ridges cut the contours at an angle. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Refer to the contour map given with Question 1.

The most appropriate description of the slope between A and B is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Contour lines show the shape of the relief: the closer together they are, the steeper the slope. Between A and B (and over the whole map) the contours are drawn very close together and almost evenly spaced, which describes a steep slope. A gentle slope would show widely spaced contours; a stepped slope would alternate close and widely spaced contours; a concave slope has contours close together near the top and wider apart near the bottom. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The figure below is for question 5. The grid reference for the shaded portion is:

![fig-2](gce-ol-geography-2021-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: A four-figure grid reference gives the easting first (the vertical grid lines, numbered along the bottom edge), then the northing (the horizontal lines, numbered up the side): along the corridor and then up the stairs. The shaded square has its lower-left (south-west) corner on easting line 46 and northing line 00, so its grid reference is 4600. 0046 reverses the order, 4647 uses lines that are not the corner of the shaded square and 0001 is not a point on the grid. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What longitude would 15°E combine with to make a great circle?
questions.corrige_markdown: A great circle divides the globe into two equal halves, so a great circle through a meridian also passes through the opposite meridian on the far side of the Earth. Two opposite meridians are 180° apart and lie on opposite sides of the Prime Meridian: 15°E is opposite 180° - 15° = 165°W (check: 15 + 165 = 180). 165°E lies on the same side as 15°E, and 75°E and 65°W do not add up to 180° with 15°E. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Water is released into the atmosphere from the following Except one. Which is this exception?
questions.corrige_markdown: Water gets into the atmosphere as vapour by evaporation from rivers and lakes (and the seas) and by transpiration from plants. Rivers (A), lakes (B) and plants (C) are all direct sources of water vapour. Ice is a frozen store of water: it releases water to the atmosphere only slowly and in small amounts (sublimation), so it is the exception the question looks for. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: From the top to the earth surface, the layers of the atmosphere are as follows:
questions.corrige_markdown: Starting from the outer layers and coming down to the ground, the layers are the thermosphere, then the mesosphere, then the stratosphere and finally the troposphere, where we live and where weather happens (the exosphere lies above the thermosphere but is not offered). Option A lists the layers from the ground upwards; B puts the stratosphere at the top and the thermosphere next to the troposphere; D puts the stratosphere above the mesosphere. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Sort out the odd statement from the information on the hydrological cycle.

*Options as printed:* A) Solar energy and precipitation are inputs in the Water cycle.   B) Overland flow and through flow are forms of run-off.   C) Through flow and base flow are all horizontal movements of water in the hydrological cycle.   D) Evaporation and through flow are processes in the hydrological cycle.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The hydrological cycle is described with inputs (precipitation, driven by solar energy), stores (oceans, ice, groundwater), flows or transfers (overland flow, throughflow, base flow, channel flow) and processes (evaporation, transpiration, condensation, infiltration). Statement A is acceptable (solar energy drives the cycle and precipitation is its water input). B is true: overland flow and throughflow are forms of run-off. C is true: throughflow in the soil and base flow from the groundwater are both horizontal movements of water. In statement D evaporation is a process but throughflow is a flow (a transfer of water), so the two are not of the same kind: this is the most likely odd statement. The wording of the options is loose, so this reading is not certain.

**Intended answer: D (Evaporation and through flow are processes in the hydrological cycle).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following are considered improper as regards the position of the school weather station and the recording of daily readings?

I. The rain gauge stands on the ground surface.

II. The school weather station is sited next to the geography room.

III. Relative humidity reading at 7:30am is entered in the column of the current day in the weather recording sheet.

IV. Maximum thermometer reading at 7:30am is entered in the column of the previous day in the recording sheet.

*Options as printed:* A) IV and I   B) I,II,III   C) II and IV   D) I,II and IV
questions.corrige_markdown:
Checking each statement against standard practice: (I) a rain gauge is set in an open space with its rim above the ground (about 30 cm) so that rain splashing from the ground is not collected; a gauge simply standing on the ground surface is improper. (II) A weather station must be in an open space away from buildings and trees, which change the wind, the temperature and the rain caught: a station next to a classroom block is improper. (III) A humidity reading is entered on the day it is read: proper. (IV) A maximum thermometer read in the morning gives the highest temperature of the previous 24 hours, so it is correctly entered under the previous day: proper. The improper statements are therefore I and II only. None of the printed options (A: IV and I; B: I, II, III; C: II and IV; D: I, II and IV) matches this exactly, so no letter can be chosen.

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the diagram of land and sea breezes below. The direction in which the wind is blowing for sea breeze is

![fig-3](gce-ol-geography-2021-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

*Options as printed:* A) WZXY.   B) WYXZ.   C) XZWY.   D) YXZW.
questions.corrige_markdown:
By day the land heats up faster than the sea. The air over the land (W) is warmed and rises, then spreads out towards the sea at height (Y). It sinks over the cooler sea (X) and comes back along the surface from the sea to the land (Z), taking the place of the rising air. This is the sea breeze (a wind from the sea to the land at the surface). The circuit is W, Y, X, Z and back to W: option B. Option A (WZXY) is the reverse circuit, the land breeze. Options C (XZWY) and D (YXZW) describe the same circuit as B but start from another letter, so the three options cannot be told apart by the circuit alone and the question is not reliable.

**Intended answer: B (WYXZ).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Refer to the diagram of land and sea breezes given with Question 11.

For land breeze the wind will blow as follows:
questions.corrige_markdown: At night the land cools faster than the sea. The air over the warmer sea (X) rises and spreads towards the land at height (Y); it sinks over the cool land (W) and returns along the surface from the land to the sea (Z), where it replaces the rising air. This is the land breeze (a wind from the land to the sea at the surface). The circuit is W, Z, X, Y and back to W: option A. Option B (XZWY) is the circuit of the sea breeze; options C (YZXW) and D (WXYZ) do not follow the loop of the diagram. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 13, 14 and 15 are based on the following table:

| Month | J | F | M | A | M | J | J | A | S | O | N | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Temp (°C) | 24 | 25 | 23 | 23 | 22 | 23 | 22 | 21.5 | 21.5 | 22 | 23 | 24 |
| Rainfall (mm) | 30 | 70 | 150 | 180 | 210 | 160 | 65 | 80 | 220 | 300 | 140 | 25 |

What type of climate do the figures in the table above represent?
questions.corrige_markdown: Read the table: the temperature stays between 21.5 °C and 25 °C all year (an annual range of only 3.5 °C), rain falls in every month, there are two rainfall peaks (210 mm in May and 300 mm in October) with a short dip in July and August, and the yearly total is about 1630 mm. A small temperature range, heavy rain in all months and two rainfall maxima describe the equatorial climate (the Cameroon type). The Mediterranean climate has a dry hot summer and winter rain; the tropical continental climate has one rainy season, a long dry season and a larger temperature range; the tropical monsoon climate has a single, very heavy rainy season. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Refer to the climate table given with Question 13.

The month with the highest total rainfall is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Compare the rainfall row: March 150 mm, May 210 mm, September 220 mm and October 300 mm. The largest value is 300 mm, in October. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Refer to the climate table given with Question 13.

What type of vegetation is most common at the place whose climate is shown by the table?
questions.corrige_markdown: The equatorial climate (hot and wet all year) supports the equatorial or tropical rainforest: tall, broad-leaved hardwood trees such as iroko and mahogany, which are evergreen as a forest because the trees lose their leaves at different times. Pine and conifers (A) belong to cold-temperate regions, teak and deciduous forest (B) to the drier monsoon and tropical lands, and birch and beech (D) to temperate deciduous forest. Option C is the one meant to describe the rainforest. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Trees like iroko, mahogany, Evergreen deciduous trees.
Trees like birch, beech temperate deciduous.

questions.enonce_markdown:
When the minimum temperature recorded in 24 hours is subtracted from the maximum, the result is:

*Options as printed:* A) The daily temperature difference.   B) The total temperature in 24 hours.   C) The diurnal range of temperature.   D) The 24 hours average temperature.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The difference between the highest (maximum) and the lowest (minimum) temperature in a day is the diurnal range of temperature, also called the daily temperature range. Options A and C name the same quantity in different words (daily = diurnal, difference = range), so the printed options do not single out one letter; the technical term is the diurnal range. A total of the temperatures (B) or an average (D) would be obtained by adding, not subtracting.

**Intended answer: C (The diurnal range of temperature).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following instrument does NOT measure the corresponding weather element?

| | Weather Element | Measuring Instrument |
|---|---|---|
| A | Rainfall | Pluviometer |
| B | Temperature | Thermometer |
| C | Humidity | Hydrometer |
| D | Atmospheric Pressure | Barometer |
questions.corrige_markdown: A pluviometer (rain gauge) measures rainfall, a thermometer measures temperature and a barometer measures atmospheric pressure. Humidity is measured with a hygrometer (or a wet and dry bulb thermometer); a hydrometer measures the density of a liquid, not the humidity of the air. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
![fig-4](gce-ol-geography-2021-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

The plate margin marked A on the diagram is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The diagram shows two plates of lithosphere moving away from each other on both sides of A, while magma wells up from the mantle (asthenosphere) into the gap and builds new oceanic crust. Plates moving apart with new crust being made form a constructive (divergent) margin, for example a mid-ocean ridge. A destructive margin has plates moving together with one being destroyed (subduction); a collision margin has two continental plates pushed together; a conservative margin has plates sliding past each other without crust being made or destroyed. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following is the correct order in the freeze-thaw process of physical weathering?

*Options as printed:* A) Rocks develop cracks; crack collects water, water freezes, volume increases, rock breaks.   B) Ice collects in cracks, opens cracks as volume increases and melts into water.   C) Water collects in cracks, freezes, volume increases, rock breaks.   D) Ice cools and freezes, breaks rocks, melts into water as volume increases.
questions.corrige_markdown:
In freeze-thaw (frost shattering) water collects in cracks of the rock. When the temperature falls below 0 °C the water freezes and its volume increases by about 9 per cent, so the ice pushes against the sides of the crack and widens it. After many cycles of freezing and thawing the rock breaks into angular pieces. Options B and D are wrong because it is water, not ice, that first enters the cracks, and ice does not 'cool' or 'break' the rock by itself. Options A and C both give a correct sequence (A also begins with the rock developing cracks), so the printed options do not single out one letter; A is the more complete one.

**Intended answer: A (Rocks develop cracks; crack collects water, water freezes, volume increases, rock breaks).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which is the odd item below?
questions.corrige_markdown: Glaciers (moving ice), wind and waves are agents of erosion: they pick up, carry and wear away rock and soil. Frost is a weather condition that causes weathering (freeze-thaw) in place, without transporting material, so it is the odd one out. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
When temperature rises and falls regularly in hot desert areas, the rocks suffer from:

*Options as printed:* A) Exfoliation.   B) Weathering.   C) Expansion and contraction.   D) Temperature changes.
questions.corrige_markdown:
In hot deserts the day is very hot and the night is cold. The rock surface expands when it is heated and contracts when it cools; the repeated stress makes the outer layers peel off like the skins of an onion, which is exfoliation (thermal weathering). The options overlap: weathering (B) is the general name, expansion and contraction (C) is the mechanism and temperature changes (D) is the cause. The effect on the rock that the question names is exfoliation.

**Intended answer: A (Exfoliation).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The process of erosion common in hot deserts is:

*Options as printed:* A) Solution.   B) Attrition.   C) Hydraulic.   D) Abrasion.
questions.corrige_markdown:
In hot deserts wind is the main agent of erosion. Sand grains blown by the wind sandblast rock surfaces, which wears them away: this is abrasion (corrasion). Solution and hydraulic action need running water, which is rare in deserts. Attrition (grains knocking against each other and wearing down) also happens in wind erosion, so options B and D are both processes of the desert; abrasion is the characteristic one.

**Intended answer: D (Abrasion).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following group of features is the result of river erosion only?
questions.corrige_markdown: Features made by river erosion include V-shaped valleys, interlocking spurs, waterfalls, rapids, bluffs, river capture (headward erosion) and meanders (cut by lateral erosion). Option A contains a delta, which is built by deposition; B contains flood plains, which are deposition features; C contains ox-bow lakes, which form when deposition seals off a meander. Option D (waterfall, river capture, meander) is the only group without a feature of deposition. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: These economic activities are concerned with Information and involve high expertise and skills. This definition best describes:
questions.corrige_markdown: Primary industries take raw materials from the earth (farming, mining, fishing); secondary industries process them (manufacturing); tertiary industries provide services (trade, transport, banking). Quaternary industries deal with information and knowledge and need highly skilled people (research and development, information technology, consultancy). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The diagram below shows the possible direction on the movement of the fault blocks.

![fig-5](gce-ol-geography-2021-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)

In what directions did the fault block move?

*Options as printed:* A) W and Z   B) X and Y   C) W and X   D) Y and Z
questions.corrige_markdown:
The block diagram shows a layered block (with a dark band) cut by a fault, and the band is not continuous across the fault: the two blocks have been displaced against each other. Four arrows are drawn: W and Z beside Block A, and X and Y beside Block B. X points upwards and Z downwards (vertical movement); W and Y are drawn along the length of the slab (horizontal movement). A movement along a fault can be vertical (one block up or down relative to the other) or horizontal (the blocks slide past each other), and the same displacement can be described by the movement of either block. The options pair arrows of the same block (W and Z, X and Y) or of different blocks (W and X, Y and Z), so several of them describe the same displacement and the drawing does not say which block moved. No letter can be chosen reliably.

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Rocks formed when sediments are buried, Compressed and cemented from organic materials are:
questions.corrige_markdown: Sedimentary rocks are of three kinds: mechanically formed (from fragments of other rocks, such as sandstone), chemically formed (from minerals that come out of solution, such as rock salt) and biologically (organically) formed from the remains of plants and animals (such as coal and some limestones). Rocks built from organic materials are biologically formed. Metamorphic rocks are rocks changed by heat and pressure, so option D is not a kind of sedimentary rock. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The vertical section of the soil showing different layers is the:
questions.corrige_markdown: A soil profile is a vertical section from the surface down to the parent rock, showing the layers (horizons) of the soil. A horizon is only one layer of the profile, structure is the way the soil particles are grouped into lumps, and texture is the proportion of sand, silt and clay. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the name of the mining method where deposits of sand and particles of useful minerals such as gold are sieved from waste.
questions.corrige_markdown: Placer mining recovers heavy minerals such as gold, tin or diamonds from loose sand and gravel (usually in river beds) by washing, panning or sieving. An adit is a horizontal tunnel driven into a hillside, a shaft is a vertical tunnel, and open cast mining removes the surface layers in a large pit. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following minerals is used to generate power?
questions.corrige_markdown: Coal is a fossil fuel: it is burned in thermal power stations to produce steam that turns turbines. Diamond is used for gems and cutting tools, copper for electric wires and gold for jewellery and reserves; none of them is a fuel. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: HEP is considered a renewable source of energy because it is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Hydro-electric power uses the energy of flowing water, which is replaced all the time by rain through the water cycle, so the source is not used up or finished after exploitation. Being cheap (C) or clean (B) are advantages but they do not make a source renewable, and transformers (A) are only equipment for the transmission of electricity. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Cheap to produce and low in consumption.
Not exhausted or finished after exploitation.

questions.enonce_markdown:
For this question, one or more of the responses given are correct. Decide which of the responses is (are) correct. Then choose:

A: If 1 and 2 only are correct. B: If 2 and 3 only are correct. C: If 1, 2, 3 are all correct. D: If 1 only is correct.

A foot loose industry

1. Has a wide variety of locations.

2. Needs good access and efficient transport.

3. Uses light raw materials.

*Options as printed:* A) If 1 and 2 only are correct.   B) If 2 and 3 only are correct.   C) If 1, 2, 3 are all correct.   D) If 1 only is correct.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A footloose industry is not tied to a particular source of raw materials or to the market, so it has a wide choice of locations (1). It uses light, small-bulk and high-value materials or components (3), and because it is free of the raw materials it depends on good access and efficient transport (roads, airports, communications) to bring in components and send out products (2). All three statements appear in the usual definition.

**Intended answer: C (If 1, 2, 3 are all correct).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 32 to 35: each question gives a First statement and a Second statement. Choose A if both statements are true, B if both are false, C if the first statement is true and the second is false, D if the first statement is false and the second is true.

**First statement:** Shipbuilding, iron/steel and brewery are all classified as heavy industries.

**Second statement:** Most heavy industries are near the source of raw materials.
questions.corrige_markdown: First statement: shipbuilding and iron and steel are heavy industries (large, bulky raw materials and products), but a brewery makes a consumer product (drink) and is generally classed as a light industry, so the statement is false. Second statement: most heavy industries are sited near their heavy, bulky raw materials (coal, iron ore) to keep transport costs low, so it is true. The first is false and the second is true. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: If both statements in Column I and II are true.
If the first statement is true and the second is false.
If the first statement is false and the second is true.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 32 to 35: each question gives a First statement and a Second statement. Choose A if both statements are true, B if both are false, C if the first statement is true and the second is false, D if the first statement is false and the second is true.

**First statement:** According to Thomas Malthus, famine is a negative check to population growth.

**Second statement:** From hamlet, village, city, conurbation is correct order settlement size.

*Options as printed:* A) If both statements in Column I and II are true.   B) If both statements are false.   C) If the first statement is true and the second is false.   D) If the first statement is false and the second is true.
questions.corrige_markdown:
First statement: Thomas Malthus (1798) argued that population grows faster than food supply and is held back by checks. He called famine, disease and war 'positive checks' because they raise the death rate, and moral restraint a 'preventive check'; some textbooks call the former 'negative checks' because they reduce the population. So the statement is true or false according to the words used in the course book. Second statement: the usual order of settlements by increasing size is hamlet, village, town, city, conurbation; the printed list leaves out 'town' but is in the right increasing order. Because the first statement depends on the wording of the textbook, no letter can be chosen reliably (with the wording 'negative checks' for famine, both statements are true, option A).

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 32 to 35: each question gives a First statement and a Second statement. Choose A if both statements are true, B if both are false, C if the first statement is true and the second is false, D if the first statement is false and the second is true.

**First statement:** Pipe lines are most secured and suitable for crude oil transportation.

**Second statement:** The greatest effect of air pollution is the destruction of marine life.
questions.corrige_markdown: First statement: true. A pipeline carries crude oil safely and cheaply over long distances without the risks of road tankers (for example the Chad-Cameroon pipeline to the coast at Kribi). Second statement: false. The greatest effects of air pollution are on human health (breathing diseases), acid rain, damage to vegetation and global warming; the destruction of marine life is mainly caused by water pollution such as oil spills. The first is true and the second is false. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: If both statements in Column I and II are true.
If the first statement is true and the second is false.
If the first statement is false and the second is true.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 32 to 35: each question gives a First statement and a Second statement. Choose A if both statements are true, B if both are false, C if the first statement is true and the second is false, D if the first statement is false and the second is true.

**First statement:** One of the causes of people moving from villages to towns is the absence of employment facilities in the villages.

**Second statement:** The practice of artificial supply of water where it is insufficient for plant growth is an aspect of land reclamation.
questions.corrige_markdown: First statement: true. The lack of jobs, schools, hospitals and other services in villages is a push factor that makes people move to towns. Second statement: true. Land reclamation means making unproductive land usable, for example by draining swamps, reclaiming land from the sea or irrigating dry land; irrigation (supplying water artificially where rainfall is not enough) is one aspect of it. Both statements are true. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: If both statements in Column I and II are true.
If the first statement is true and the second is false.
If the first statement is false and the second is true.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following represents a physical factor of tourism?
questions.corrige_markdown: Physical (natural) factors of tourism are attractions that nature provides: scenery, climate, beaches, mountains and wildlife. Human factors are things people build or maintain: buildings, hotels, culture and transport. The Prime Minister's Lodge in Buea, the Palace of the Sultan in Foumban and the Sawa Hotel in Douala are man-made. The gorilla sanctuary is a natural wildlife attraction. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: The Prime Minister's Lodge in Buea.
The Palace of the Sultan in Foumban.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the urban problem below that does NOT agree with its corresponding solution.
questions.corrige_markdown: Traffic congestion is eased by building by-passes, high land values by building council housing, and disused factory buildings can be turned into science and business parks. Dumping waste into streams is not a solution to the problem of waste disposal: it pollutes the water and spreads disease. Proper solutions are collection, recycling, controlled landfill or incineration. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Waste disposal / dumping waste into streams.
High land values / construction of local council accommodation.
Disused factory buildings / development of science and business parks.

questions.enonce_markdown: Who amongst these persons in a settlement is most affected by the statement: "extra noise by factories frighten away wild life?"
questions.corrige_markdown: Environmentalists are concerned with protecting wildlife and the natural environment, so noise that drives animals away affects them most. Farmers, teenagers and elderly persons are affected by noise in other ways but not mainly through the loss of wildlife. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Densely populated area means:
questions.corrige_markdown: Population density is the number of people living in a unit of area, usually per square kilometre. A densely populated area therefore has many people per square kilometre. 'Crowded' (A) and 'many people' (C) do not take the size of the area into account, and the size of the place being 'thick' (B) has no meaning. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: The size of the place is thick.
The number of people per square kilometre.

questions.enonce_markdown: When Birth rate is more than death rate the population:
questions.corrige_markdown: The natural change of a population is the birth rate minus the death rate. When births are more than deaths (and migration is ignored) there are more people each year, so the population increases. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A 16 year old school girl living in a village sustained a severe injury in an accident. Her parents decided to take her to the city. Suggest the most likely reason for the movement.
questions.corrige_markdown: A severe injury needs urgent treatment, and hospitals with doctors, equipment and ambulances are mostly found in cities, while villages often have only small health centres. The movement is therefore for effective medical care. Jobs, education or marriage would not explain taking an injured girl to the city straight after an accident. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Hope for better education in the city.
Family desires her to get married.

questions.enonce_markdown: There are many varieties of soil in Cameroon, the azonal soils include:
questions.corrige_markdown: Azonal soils are young soils that have not had time to develop a profile, so they reflect their parent material or the way they were deposited rather than the climate and vegetation of the zone. Alluvial soils (river deposits) and volcanic soils (for example around Mount Cameroon) are azonal. Ferrallitic and ferruginous soils are zonal soils: they are the soils of the equatorial and the tropical climates. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the watershed from which River Benue and Sanaga take their rise.
questions.corrige_markdown: The Adamawa High Plateau is the main water-parting of Cameroon: the Benue rises on it near Ngaoundere and flows towards Nigeria, and the headstreams of the Sanaga (the Lom and the Djerem) also come from the Adamawa. The Western Highlands feed rivers such as the Wouri and the Noun, the South Cameroon plateau feeds rivers such as the Nyong and the Ntem, and the Mandara Mountains feed small rivers of the north. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the map of Cameroon provided and answer questions 44 to 46.

![fig-6](gce-ol-geography-2021-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_6.png)

Into what drainage basin does river "R" empties its water?
questions.corrige_markdown: On the sketch map the river R is drawn in the western part of the northern region and it flows west across the frontier. This is the course of the Benue, which rises on the Adamawa Plateau, flows into Nigeria and joins the Niger, so the river drains into the Niger basin. The Atlantic basin takes the rivers of the south and west (Sanaga, Wouri, Nyong), the Chad basin takes rivers of the far north (Logone), and the Congo basin takes the rivers of the south-east. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Refer to the map of Cameroon given with Question 44.

Identify the climatic zone north of the line X-Y.
questions.corrige_markdown: On the sketch map the line X-Y marks the southern limit of the northern region, the hatched region II lying south of it. North of this line Cameroon has the tropical (Sudan) climate: hot, with one long rainy season and a long dry season. The south has the equatorial (Guinea) climate with rain in most months. A Sahara climate is not found in Cameroon. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Refer to the map of Cameroon given with Question 44.

The towns B, A, Z respectively are
questions.corrige_markdown: B is the town in the middle of the northern region, on the Adamawa Plateau: Ngaoundere. A is the town at the extreme north tip of the map, near Lake Chad: Kousseri. Z lies south of A in the Far North: Maroua. The order B, A, Z is therefore Ngaoundere, Kousseri, Maroua. Garoua (option C) is further south than Maroua, on the Benue. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The total rainfall of Debundscha is higher than Muyuka though they are almost on the same latitude. This is so because:
questions.corrige_markdown: Debundscha lies on the south-western, windward foot of Mount Cameroon. The moist south-west monsoon from the Atlantic is forced to rise over the mountain, cools and gives very heavy relief rainfall, making it one of the wettest places in Africa. Muyuka is on the leeward (rain-shadow) side of the mountain, where the air has already lost much of its moisture. Since both places are at about the same latitude, latitude is not the cause. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Debunscha is on the windward slope while Muyuka is on the lee ward slope.
Muyuka is on the windward slope while Debundscha is on the lee ward slope.
Debundscha is on the higher altitude than Muyuka.
Muyuka is on the higher altitude than Debundscha.

questions.enonce_markdown: In Cameroon, movement of persons from Western High Plateaus to the Coastal Region is referred to as
questions.corrige_markdown: Moving from one region of a country to another is inter-regional migration: here people leave the Western High Plateaus and go to the Coastal Region. Rural-urban migration (A) and urban-rural migration (D) describe the type of place left and reached, which the question does not give. 'Regional migration' (B) is not the usual term for a move between two regions. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the informal sector in Cameroon?

*Options as printed:* A) Evade taxes.   B) Employ.   C) Are independent.   D) Produce affordable goods.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The informal sector is made up of small businesses that are not registered with the State, such as roadside traders, mechanics, tailors and hawkers. They use little capital and simple tools, are run independently (often by a family), employ many people and sell cheap goods and services; many of them do not pay formal taxes. All four printed options (evade taxes, employ, are independent, produce affordable goods) are features usually quoted for the informal sector, so none of them can be picked as the exception.

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: As far as tourism is involved it is often said that "Cameroon is Africa in miniature" This means that:
questions.corrige_markdown: Cameroon is called Africa in miniature because it brings together in one country most of the natural and human features of the continent: equatorial forest, savanna and semi-desert, mountains and volcanoes, a coast with beaches, plateaux, lakes and rivers, and many different peoples and cultures (over 200 ethnic groups). This variety gives the country a large and varied tourist potential. The saying says nothing about the climate being good all the year (B), the roads (C) or industry and hotels (D). **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: It offers a large tourist potential.
The climate is good for tourism throughout the year.
The government has developed good roads for tourist movement.
Everything about the country from industry and hotels attracts the tourist.
